prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map supports a coarse layered layout: the bearded man and the shoes he holds are generally the nearest central elements, roughly 0.4–1.0 m from the camera, while clothing rails and the windowed wall lie farther away at about 1.5–4 m; mannequins and other people occupy intermediate depths around 1–2.5 m. Across the five frames, the man shifts from left/centre to very close in front of the wearer and then partly out of view, while a raised shoe repeatedly projects nearer than his torso; nearby people and mannequins alternate between the left and right background as the camera turns. The bright foreground regions make arm's-reach surfaces clearer than RGB alone, including the held shoe, portions of the man's upper body, and the partial arm or hand entering at the far right, although exact person-to-person distances and facing direction are not encoded. Depth near silhouettes, the ceiling, frame boundaries, and overlapping bodies, shoes, and racks is smoothed or inconsistent, so some background areas appear implausibly close and fine occlusions are unreliable.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map separates multiple people from shoes, clothing/display structures, and a small sports-ball label, showing that people occupy the left edge, central foreground, and right side at different times, with several bodies partially outside the image or hidden behind one another. In the RGB context, the central bearded man is roughly 0.5–1.2 m from the wearer, the held shoes are within his arm's reach and sometimes within about 0.5–0.8 m of the camera, while mannequins or other people and the racks are mostly about 1–3 m away; the map itself provides ordering and overlap rather than metric distance. Over the five frames, the central person grows and shifts across the view as the camera and person change relative orientation, a large person-shaped region becomes extremely close near the middle-right, and later figures are split between a partly visible lower-centre person and a large right-side person. The masks make occlusion boundaries and partly cropped figures easier to see than in RGB, but several instances merge with nearby objects, body regions receive inconsistent colours, shoes or clothing are mislabeled or unlabeled, and the sports-ball detection appears unreliable; facing and gaze cannot be determined confidently from these masks alone.
descriptions.pose: The pose map provides sparse body and hand landmarks: yellow joints trace an extended arm and bent upper body in the early frames, while magenta landmarks isolate a raised hand near the centre and two hands near the far right in later frames. Registered to the RGB, these landmarks place the bearded man about 0.5–1.2 m in front of the wearer, with his raised hand or shoe approximately at head-to-chest height and within roughly 0.4–0.8 m of the camera; the rightmost hand cluster is also likely within about a metre, while most other people are too incomplete for dependable ranging. The changing joint locations show the visible arm moving from leftward extension to a more central raised configuration, followed by loss of most of the body as it becomes occluded or leaves the field, while a separate pair of hands appears on the right. Pose can reveal limb orientation, hand configuration, and which body parts overlap even when RGB texture is confusing, but many joints are missing or assigned to isolated points, so full-body facing, gaze direction, behind-versus-in-front relationships, and reach between different people are unreliable.
